site.title: The Villageless Mama — A sanctuary for postpartum
site.description: A quiet, ad-free digital village for postpartum mothers. Rituals, essays, breathing, audio sanctuary.

home.heading:
A village made of paper,
made for you.
home.subheading: For the mother awake at 2:30am with a baby on her chest. For the mother who was promised a village and met silence instead. Here is a small one, in your pocket.
home.welcomeP1: Somewhere along the way, we forgot how to gather around a new mother. We sent flowers. We sent silence. We sent her home, alone with a small body and a self she no longer recognised. This place is a paper village — slow, quiet, made of essays and rituals and the kind of audio that doesn't ask anything of you.
home.welcomeP2: There are no popups here. No tracking. No bright red badges. Read what you need. Close the tab when the baby stirs. Come back the next night, and the next.
home.readDesc: For the inner life, in the dark.
home.breatheDesc: A forest that breathes with you.
home.guidesDesc: Tap a guide to read it here. No checkout. No accounts.
home.guide1Desc: A 14-day gentle plan for the first weeks at home.
home.guide1Body1: Day 1–3: horizontal. Bed, water, skin-to-skin. Visitors can wait.
home.guide1Body2: Day 4–7: notice the milk wave and the tears that ride with it. Both are biology.
home.guide1Body3: Week 2: one chair, one window, one sentence to the baby per day.
home.guide1Body4: Week 3: a five-minute walk counts. Stop before tired.
home.guide1Body5: Beyond: healing keeps its own calendar. You are not behind.
home.guide2Body1: Dim the screen. One hand on chest, one on belly. Exhale longer than you inhale.
home.guide2Body2: Hum if sound helps. Silence if it doesn't.
home.guide2Body3: Feed, fold, or simply sit — the ritual is presence, not productivity.
home.guide2Body4: When the baby stirs, close this tab without guilt. The night will return tomorrow.
home.guide3Body1: Dear body, you opened. You are closing again, slowly.
home.guide3Body2: I will not rush you to look like before. Before did not know this child.
home.guide3Body3: Soft food. Warm water. Horizontal hours when you can.
home.guide3Body4: You are not failing. You are remaking.

recovery.title: Recovery Room — The Villageless Mama
recovery.description: Gentle, day-by-day notes for physical postpartum healing.
recovery.heading: Your body is healing on its own clock.
recovery.lede: A slow map of the first weeks. Use it as a permission slip.
recovery.day1Body: Bed. Pads. Water beside you. Skin-to-skin. Nothing else is required.
recovery.day2Body: The 'baby blues' wave. Notice the milk-let-down emotion. Tears are biology.
recovery.day3Body: Bleeding shifts colour. Sitz baths. Soft food. Short windows on a chair.
recovery.day4Body: Pelvic floor remembers itself slowly. Breathe down before you stand.
recovery.day5Body: Light walks at your own threshold. Stop before tired.
recovery.day6Body: Healing is not a deadline. You will keep softening for a year.
recovery.comfort1Body: Warm water, epsom salt, 10 minutes. Three times a day if you can. The perineum heals faster in warm water.
recovery.comfort2Body: It will feel impossible. It is not. Stool softener, a squat stool, and a hand on your belly. Breathe out slowly. Do not push.
recovery.comfort3Body: Cold cabbage leaves in the bra. Strange but true. Ice packs after feeding. Warmth only before, never after.
recovery.comfort4Body: Fever, foul-smelling discharge, bleeding that soaks a pad in an hour, pain that worsens instead of easing. You are not bothering anyone.

nursery.title: Nursery — The Villageless Mama
nursery.description: Small practical rituals for the baby: bathing, swaddling, the ritual of fabric.
nursery.heading: Small rituals, repeated softly.
nursery.lede: The baby learns the world from your hands.
nursery.ritual1Body: Warm cloth, warm room. Begin at the eyes, end at the feet. The order matters more than the soap.
nursery.ritual2Body: One cloth for sleep. One for play. Washed in the same water as yours. Familiar scent is a kind of safety.
nursery.ritual3Body: Lay the cloth in a diamond. Fold the top corner. Place the baby. Snug the arms. Quiet the hands.
nursery.ritual4Body: While they nurse or sleep. Use the soft file, not the clipper, for the first weeks.
nursery.ritual5Body: Dim → wipe → cream → sing one line, the same line, always. Repetition is the lullaby.
nursery.ritual6Body: Tie the carrier while standing. Bend your knees, not your back. The baby should be high enough to kiss. Tight enough to feel their breath, loose enough to move.
nursery.ritual7Body: On your chest counts. On a soft mat counts. Thirty seconds counts. The floor is not a test.
nursery.ritual8Body: They do not understand the words. They understand your voice. Read anything — a recipe, a poem, the news. The rhythm matters, not the content.

crisis.title: Crisis Room — The Villageless Mama
crisis.description: When everything is too much: ambient audio, quick troubleshooting, and permission reminders.
crisis.heading: Breathe. You're here now.
crisis.lede: A few quiet tools, gathered. Use one, or all.
crisis.ambientTitle: Choose a sound to hold the room.
crisis.a1: Check: hungry, hot, hurting, tired, lonely. If all five are no, hold them, walk slowly, hum. You are not failing.
crisis.a2: Sit down. One hand on your chest, one on your belly. Exhale longer than you inhale. This wave will pass through you, not break you.
crisis.a3: Unlatch with your little finger. Bring baby to breast, not breast to baby. Wider mouth, chin first, deeper pull.
crisis.q4: I can't sleep even when they sleep
crisis.a4: Don't force it. Lie down. Close your eyes. Rest counts. Sleep will come back.
crisis.q5: I feel rage toward the baby
crisis.a5: This is one of the most common and most hidden feelings of early motherhood. Put the baby down in a safe place. Step outside or into another room for five minutes. You are not a bad mother. You are an exhausted one.
crisis.a6: Bonding is not instant for everyone. It grows in the quiet moments — the 3am feeds, the weight of them on your chest, the first time they look at you and seem to know you. Give it time. It will come.
crisis.a7: They cannot understand. They have not been through this. Tell them what you need in one sentence. 'I need you to bring me water without asking.' 'I need you to hold the baby so I can shower.' Repeat the sentence until it lands.

quiet.title: Quiet Room — The Villageless Mama
quiet.description: A somatic breathing pacer with a forest that breathes with you.
quiet.desc446: A 4-4-6 rhythm. The forest turns green as you inhale, warm as you release.
quiet.desc478: A 4-7-8 rhythm. A classic calming pattern. Exhale longer to relax the nervous system.
quiet.descBox: Box breathing: 4-4-4-4. Used by Navy SEALs and new mothers alike.
quiet.descSimple: A gentle 4-6 rhythm. Inhale, then a long slow release. Nothing else required.

mind.title: Mother's Mind — The Villageless Mama
mind.description: Essays on womanhood, care, and the inner life of a mother.
mind.heading: Essays for the inner life.
mind.lede: Read one in the dark. Close it when you're done.
mind.essay1Sub: On becoming the woman who already exists inside you.
mind.essay1Body1: There is a word for what is happening to you. It is older than the internet, older than the hospital. Matrescence. Like adolescence, but quieter, more private, and far less prepared for.
mind.essay1Body2: Your hormones are doing what they did at thirteen. Your sense of self is unstitching to make room. The grief is real. The widening is real. So is the woman on the other side.
mind.essay1Body3: You are not losing yourself. You are doubling.
mind.essay2Body1: The fridge hums. The kettle ticks. The baby is finally heavy on your shoulder, breathing the breath of the truly asleep.
mind.essay2Body2: No one will ever know this hour but you. Not even the child you held through it.
mind.essay2Body3: Let it count. Let it count.
mind.essay3Body1: You spent the day giving care in increments smaller than a teaspoon. Now sit. Let the water be warm. Let someone else hand you the towel, if there is someone. If there isn't, hand it to yourself, slowly, like you mean it.

privacy.title: Zero Data Promise — The Villageless Mama
privacy.description: Our zero-tracking policy and the optional Face ID secure lock for private rooms.
privacy.heading: A zero-data promise.
privacy.noDataTitle: No analytics. No cookies. No third-party trackers.
privacy.noDataBody: We do not store your reading. We do not know who you are. The only data this app keeps is your theme preference and the Secure Lock setting — both live on your device, never on a server.
privacy.secureLockBody: A soft veil over the private rooms — Mother's Mind and the Crisis Room. When someone else picks up your phone, they meet a quiet threshold instead of your reflections.
privacy.footer: Last gentle review: this season. Questions live with the writer, not a corporation.
